titlePlain: TOGAF, and Where Security Fits Into
subtitle: Lesson 6 · Security Architecture Frameworks

code:
TOGAF — maintained by The Open Group (vendor-neutral
consortium), the most widely adopted EA framework

Four domains (BDAT):
  Business      - strategy, governance, processes
  Data          - logical/physical data assets
  Application   - systems and their interactions
  Technology    - hardware, software, network
caption: TOGAF starts from the whole enterprise architecture practice, not business attributes alone.

TOGAF Series Guide: Integrating Risk and Security:
  security = a CROSS-CUTTING CONCERN

  Phase A -> security objectives in the vision
  Phase D -> security services in tech architecture
  Phase G -> compliance reviews check conformance
caption: Addressed inside every phase, not bolted on at the end.

code:
TOGAF  = process framework  (HOW the practice runs)
SABSA  = content framework  (WHAT the architecture
                              should contain)

Joint Open Group / SABSA Institute guidance:
  SABSA's layers + Business Attributes Profile
  fill the security content inside each ADM phase
caption: Not competitors — TOGAF supplies the cadence, SABSA supplies the substance.
